P.title: Pipeline width (sustained NOPs per cycle)
P.note: NOPs use no execution unit, so this is the narrowest of fetch, decode, rename and retire. It bounds every other rate on this page.

P.title: Register moves per cycle (mov x, x)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent register moves over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 10.00.

P.title: Integer ALUs (add with immediate)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent add-immediate instructions over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 7.70.

P.title: Integer adds with two register sources
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent register-register adds whose sources rotate through eight registers over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 6.79.

P.title: Integer adds that all read one register
P.note: Highest sustained rate of add xN, x19, x19 (every instance reads the same register twice) over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.04. Not close to an integer: the unit count is probably the next integer up, not reached because of scheduler balancing.

P.title: Flag-setting ALUs (cmp with immediate)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent compares over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

P.title: Integer multipliers
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent multiplies over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.00.

P.title: Load units (L1 hits)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent loads that hit the L1 cache over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.00.

P.title: Store units
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent stores to distinct addresses over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 2.00.

P.title: FP adders (fadd)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent scalar fadd over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

P.title: FP multipliers (fmul)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent scalar fmul over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

P.title: SIMD integer units (add v.2d)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of independent vector integer adds over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

P.title: Not-taken conditional branches per cycle (cbz)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of never-taken cbz over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 2.30.

P.title: Taken branches per cycle (b to next)
P.note: Highest sustained rate of unconditional branches to the next instruction over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 1.47.

P.title: Reorder buffer capacity in NOPs
P.note: NOPs need no register and no scheduler entry, only room in the reorder buffer. Apple cores pack several such instructions into one reorder-buffer entry, so this is far more than the number of ordinary instructions that fit. Overlap is lost between 3358 and 3368 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.54); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Integer register renames in flight
P.note: Each filler writes an integer register, so each holds a fresh physical register until it retires. Add the 31 architectural registers for the file's total size. Overlap is lost between 396 and 397 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.79); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: 32-bit integer register renames in flight
P.note: Fillers write w registers. If this is about twice the 64-bit figure, two 32-bit values share one physical register. Overlap is lost between 809 and 811 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.69); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: FP/SIMD register renames in flight
P.note: Each filler writes a vector register. Add the 32 architectural registers for the file's total size. Overlap is lost between 836 and 838 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.53).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Flag renames in flight
P.note: Each filler (cmp) writes only NZCV. Overlap is lost between 167 and 168 fillers (time ratio 1.02 -> 1.88).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Unresolved-branch capacity
P.note: Fillers are never-taken cbz instructions. Overlap is lost between 194 and 195 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.81).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Store queue
P.note: Fillers are stores, which hold a store-queue entry until after retirement. Overlap is lost between 137 and 138 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.81).
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Load queue
P.note: Fillers are FP loads that hit the L1 cache; they finish at once but hold their load-queue entry until retirement. Overlap is lost between 483 and 485 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.58); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Reorder buffer capacity in ordinary instructions
P.note: Fillers are a blend of integer adds, FP adds, compares, never-taken branches and stores, in proportion to the capacity measured for each, so that none of those structures fills before the others. Overlap is lost between 1327 and 1330 fillers (time ratio 1.01 -> 1.66); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
P.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

P.title: Latency of mov x, x fed by an add
P.note: Chain of add + mov takes 1.00 cycles per step against 1.00 for the add alone. Zero means the move is eliminated at rename.

P.title: Latency of mov x, x fed by another mov
P.note: Each extra move in a run of moves adds this much (chains of 3 and 9 moves: 2.80 and 8.19 cycles per step). A value just below 1 means a move whose source is itself a move renamed in the same cycle is executed, not eliminated.

P.title: Latency of mov x0, x0
P.note: add + mov x0, x0 takes 1.00 cycles per step (add alone: 1.00).

P.title: Latency of add x, x, #0
P.note: add x1, x0, #1 ; add x0, x1, #0 takes 1.00 cycles per step (add alone: 1.00). Zero means add #0 is treated as a move.

P.title: Latency of mov v.16b, v.16b fed by a vector add
P.note: Chain of add v.2d + mov v takes 2.00 cycles per step against 2.00 for the add alone.

P.title: Latency of mov v.16b, v.16b fed by another mov
P.note: Each extra vector move in a run of moves adds this much (chains of 3 and 9: 5.60 and 16.38 cycles per step).

P.title: Latency of fmov d, d fed by a vector add
P.note: Chain of add v.2d + fmov d, d takes 4.00 cycles per step against 2.00 for the add alone. fmov d, d must clear the upper 64 bits, so it is not a plain rename.

P.title: eor x0, x0, x0 inside a multiply chain
P.note: Cycles per step of mul x0, x0, x20 followed by the idiom. The multiply alone takes 3.00; a value below that means the idiom broke the dependency on x0, a value above it means the idiom was executed as an ordinary operation (4.00).

P.title: sub x0, x0, x0 inside a multiply chain
P.note: Cycles per step of mul x0, x0, x20 followed by the idiom. The multiply alone takes 3.00; a value below that means the idiom broke the dependency on x0, a value above it means the idiom was executed as an ordinary operation (4.00).

P.title: cmp + b.cond
P.note: cmp x19, x20 ; b.eq. With 5 adds per block, 1.25 blocks per cycle when the pair is adjacent and 1.09 when one add separates it. The adjacent form needs fewer execution slots: the pair is fused.

P.title: Branch misprediction penalty
P.note: One iteration takes 1.50 cycles when the branch alternates and 9.92 when it follows random bits; twice the difference is the cost of one misprediction, assuming half of the random branches are mispredicted (that rate cannot be read without PMU events, hence the confidence). The branch's condition is ready before it is renamed, so this is the shortest penalty the pipeline has.

P.title: L1 load-to-use latency (pointer chase)
P.note: ldr x1, [x1] over a buffer of 16 to 32 KiB. Register-offset addressing adds a cycle (see the instruction table).

P.title: L1 data cache capacity
P.note: Largest buffer that still loads in 3.0 cycles; the next size tried (135 KiB) is slower. The OS reports 128 KiB.

P.title: L2 load-to-use latency, small footprint
P.note: Pointer chase over 256 to 512 KiB: past the L1 cache and still covered by the first-level TLB.

P.title: L2 load-to-use latency, large footprint
P.note: Pointer chase over 2048 to 8192 KiB. Includes first-level TLB misses where the footprint exceeds the TLB's reach.

P.title: L2 cache capacity seen by one core
P.note: Latency passes twice the large-footprint L2 latency between 16384 and 23170 KiB. The OS reports 16384 KiB shared by 4 cores; the other cores were busy, so one core sees less than the whole cache.

P.title: Load latency from memory (128 MiB random chase)
P.note: 351 cycles at the clock observed; includes TLB misses (16 KiB pages). Depends on the memory fitted and on what else uses it.

P.title: First-level data TLB entries
P.note: One cell per 16 KiB page against the same cells packed together: translation is free up to 162 pages and costs more from 166 on.
P.ylabel: extra cycles per load (one cell per page)

P.title: Second-level TLB entries
P.note: A first-level TLB miss that the second level catches costs about 6.0 cycles. From 3170 pages on (3101 were still fine) the cost passes 12.0 cycles: page walks. See the first-level entry for the curve.

P.title: Latency of a load that always returns the same value
P.note: ldr x0, [x0] chasing a cell that points to itself takes 0.34 cycles per load; the same load walking a ring of 509 cells takes 3.03. The constant value is predicted, so the chain no longer waits for the load: a self-pointing cell cannot be used to measure load latency here. The curve shows how many alternating values are still predicted.
P.xlabel: distinct values each load returns in turn

P.title: add + csel chained through the input csel does not select
P.note: add x1, x0, #1 ; csel x0, x21, x1, ne with the flags never written, so x21 is always chosen. Cycles per step, smallest of five placements (0.30 to 0.60, mean 0.43). 2 means the select waited for the input it did not choose; well below 1 means that dependency no longer exists and the loop runs at throughput speed.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: The same chain after 64 iterations of the opposite outcome
P.note: Identical code at new addresses, with 64 iterations of the opposite condition between training and measurement. P.title: The same chain with csinc (control)

P.title: Latency of csel when its condition has never changed

P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Latency of the same csel after 64 iterations of the other outcome

P.title: Latency of csinc under the same conditions (control)

P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Latency of mov x0, x1 in the same loops (reference)
P.note: What a fully eliminated move looks like in this loop. Smallest of five placements of the select; they ranged from 0.00 to 0.00 (mean 0.00). 1 is ordinary data flow; less than 1 means that some of the selects did not cost a cycle.
P.xlabel: NOPs between the add and the select

P.title: Two serialised cache misses when the data are pointers
P.note: Two independent chases, each missing the cache, with 1000 adds between them so that the second cannot enter the window until the first retires. Relative to a loop with one chase this costs 1.68x when the cells hold indices and 1.37x when they hold pointers. The pointers are being dereferenced ahead of the program: a data-memory-dependent prefetcher is at work, and it hides the second miss.

E.title: Pipeline width (sustained NOPs per cycle)
E.note: NOPs use no execution unit, so this is the narrowest of fetch, decode, rename and retire. It bounds every other rate on this page.

E.title: Register moves per cycle (mov x, x)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent register moves over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 6.00.

E.title: Integer ALUs (add with immediate)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent add-immediate instructions over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

E.title: Integer adds with two register sources
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent register-register adds whose sources rotate through eight registers over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

E.title: Integer adds that all read one register
E.note: Highest sustained rate of add xN, x19, x19 (every instance reads the same register twice) over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

E.title: Flag-setting ALUs (cmp with immediate)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent compares over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 4.00.

E.title: Integer multipliers
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent multiplies over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 1.00.

E.title: Load units (L1 hits)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent loads that hit the L1 cache over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 2.00.

E.title: Store units
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent stores to distinct addresses over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 1.00.

E.title: FP adders (fadd)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent scalar fadd over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.00.

E.title: FP multipliers (fmul)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent scalar fmul over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.00.

E.title: SIMD integer units (add v.2d)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of independent vector integer adds over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 3.00.

E.title: Not-taken conditional branches per cycle (cbz)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of never-taken cbz over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 2.00.

E.title: Taken branches per cycle (b to next)
E.note: Highest sustained rate of unconditional branches to the next instruction over all dilutions with NOPs; an undiluted stream reaches 1.00.

E.title: Reorder buffer capacity in NOPs
E.note: NOPs need no register and no scheduler entry, only room in the reorder buffer. Apple cores pack several such instructions into one reorder-buffer entry, so this is far more than the number of ordinary instructions that fit. Overlap is lost between 1064 and 1067 fillers (time ratio 0.92 -> 1.61); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: Integer register renames in flight
E.note: Each filler writes an integer register, so each holds a fresh physical register until it retires. Add the 31 architectural registers for the file's total size. Overlap is lost between 182 and 183 fillers (time ratio 0.92 -> 1.71); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: 32-bit integer register renames in flight
E.note: Fillers write w registers. If this is about twice the 64-bit figure, two 32-bit values share one physical register. Overlap is lost between 183 and 184 fillers (time ratio 0.93 -> 1.79); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: FP/SIMD register renames in flight
E.note: Each filler writes a vector register. Add the 32 architectural registers for the file's total size. Overlap is lost between 202 and 203 fillers (time ratio 0.91 -> 1.76).
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: Flag renames in flight
E.note: Each filler (cmp) writes only NZCV. Overlap is lost between 72 and 74 fillers (time ratio 0.95 -> 1.90).
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: Unresolved-branch capacity
E.note: Fillers are never-taken cbz instructions. Overlap is lost between 72 and 74 fillers (time ratio 0.96 -> 1.79).
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: Store queue
E.note: Fillers are stores, which hold a store-queue entry until after retirement. Overlap is lost between 55 and 56 fillers (time ratio 0.99 -> 1.85).
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: Load queue
E.note: Fillers are FP loads that hit the L1 cache; they finish at once but hold their load-queue entry until retirement. Overlap is lost between 62 and 64 fillers (time ratio 0.97 -> 1.90); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.title: Reorder buffer capacity in ordinary instructions
E.note: Fillers are a blend of integer adds, FP adds, compares, never-taken branches and stores, in proportion to the capacity measured for each, so that none of those structures fills before the others. Overlap is lost between 464 and 465 fillers (time ratio 0.94 -> 1.64); the blocker's own instructions are added to the count.
E.xlabel: filler instructions between the two misses

E.note: fmul alone takes 3.50 cycles per step; below that means the dependency was broken (6.00).
